title: A Survey of Self-Evolving Agents: On Path to Artificial Super Intelligence
note: Surveys what, when, and how foundation-model agents can evolve across models, memory, tools, and architectures. (TMLR 2026)

title: Recursive Self-Improvement in AI: From Bounded Self-Refinement to Autonomous Research Loops
note: Surveys recent self-improvement work by update target and loop closure while separating bounded refinement from open-ended RSI. (arXiv 2026)

title: EvoLM: Self-Evolving Language Models through Co-Evolved Discriminative Rubrics
note: Alternately trains one model to generate discriminative rubrics and improve its policy from rubric-conditioned rewards without human annotations or external reward models. (arXiv 2026)

title: RLAIF vs. RLHF: Scaling Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback with AI Feedback
note: Studies reinforcement learning from AI-generated preferences as a scalable alternative to direct human feedback. (ICML 2024)

title: Automated Design of Agentic Systems
note: Uses a meta-agent to invent and iteratively improve agent architectures represented as executable code. (ICLR 2025)

title: TextGrad: Automatic "Differentiation" via Text
note: Backpropagates textual feedback through compound AI systems to optimize prompts, code, and other textual variables. (Nature 2025)

title: Language Agent Tree Search Unifies Reasoning, Acting, and Planning in Language Models
note: Combines Monte Carlo tree search, model-based value estimates, environment feedback, and self-reflection without updating base weights. (ICML 2024)

title: Large Language Models as Optimizers
note: Introduces OPRO, which iteratively proposes and evaluates natural-language solutions and prompts from a history of scored attempts. (ICLR 2024)

title: Promptbreeder: Self-Referential Self-Improvement Via Prompt Evolution
note: Evolves both task prompts and the mutation prompts that generate future prompt improvements. (ICML 2024)

title: Self-Taught Optimizer (STOP): Recursively Self-Improving Code Generation
note: Demonstrates an LLM-written scaffolding program that improves the program responsible for making further improvements. (COLM 2024)

title: DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into Self-Improving Pipelines
note: Compiles declarative LM programs by optimizing prompts and demonstrations against a user-defined metric. (NeurIPS 2023 R0-FoMo Workshop)

title: Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models
note: Evolves context as a structured playbook through generation, reflection, and curation while avoiding destructive context collapse. (ICLR 2026)

title: EvolveR: Self-Evolving LLM Agents through an Experience-Driven Lifecycle
note: Distills interaction trajectories into reusable strategic principles, retrieves them during future tasks, and reinforces the agent policy in a closed experience loop. (ICML 2026)

title: From Procedural Skills to Strategy Genes: Towards Experience-Driven Test-Time Evolution
note: Compares experience representations across 4,590 controlled trials and finds that compact, editable Genes provide stronger test-time control and carry accumulated failure history better than documenta

title: Learning to Continually Learn via Meta-learning Agentic Memory Designs
note: Uses a meta-agent to discover executable memory schemas and retrieval and update mechanisms that continually improve from experience. (arXiv 2026)

title: A-MEM: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents
note: Builds a dynamically linked note network whose organization evolves as an agent accumulates new experiences. (NeurIPS 2025)

title: ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners
note: Extracts reusable insights from successful and failed trajectories and transfers them to future tasks without weight updates. (AAAI 2024)

title: MemoryBank: Enhancing Large Language Models with Long-Term Memory
note: Maintains and selectively forgets long-term interaction memories so an agent can adapt its responses over time. (AAAI 2024)

title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
note: Improves agents across trials by storing natural-language reflections derived from task feedback. (NeurIPS 2023)

title: Agentic Harness Engineering: Observability-Driven Automatic Evolution of Coding-Agent Harnesses
note: Autonomously evolves tools, middleware, memory, and prompts through observable edits whose predictions are verified on later tasks. (arXiv 2026)

title: Agent0: Unleashing Self-Evolving Agents from Zero Data via Tool-Integrated Reasoning
note: Co-evolves curriculum and executor agents initialized from the same base model to improve tool-using reasoning without human-curated data. (arXiv 2025)

title: DEBATE, TRAIN, EVOLVE: Self Evolution of Language Model Reasoning
note: Fine-tunes a model on its own multi-agent debate traces and repeats the debate-training loop without ground-truth labels. (EMNLP 2025)

title: EvoAgent: Towards Automatic Multi-Agent Generation via Evolutionary Algorithms
note: Applies mutation, crossover, and selection to expand a specialized agent into a diverse multi-agent system. (NAACL 2025)

title: SOTOPIA-π: Interactive Learning of Socially Intelligent Language Agents
note: Improves an agent policy through behavior cloning and self-reinforcement on filtered multi-agent social interactions. (ACL 2024)

title: Darwin Gödel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents
note: Evolves a coding agent by modifying its own code and retaining empirically validated improvements in an open-ended archive. (ICLR 2026)

title: A Self-Improving Coding Agent
note: Demonstrates a coding agent that edits its own implementation and empirically improves on SWE-bench Verified. (ICLR 2025 SSI-FM Workshop)

title: Training Software Engineering Agents and Verifiers with SWE-Gym
note: Supplies executable repository tasks and trajectories for training both SWE agents and inference-time verifiers. (ICML 2025)

title: Teaching Large Language Models to Self-Debug
note: Teaches models to inspect execution results, explain their code, and repair failures through iterative prompting. (ICLR 2024)

title: AutoResearch: Insight In, Hallucination Out
note: Connects grounded idea generation with coordinated execution agents that implement, diagnose, and independently review experiments before accepting research conclusions. (arXiv 2026)

title: Frontis-MA1: Training an AI4AI Model towards Recursive Self-Improvement in Machine Learning Engineering
note: Connects execution-grounded operator training with long-horizon evolution in the open OpenMLE stack, using machine-learning engineering as an AI4AI testbed for RSI. (arXiv 2026)

title: FT-Dojo: Towards Autonomous LLM Fine-Tuning with Language Agents
note: Turns data collection, training, evaluation, diagnosis, and strategy revision into an executable environment for autonomous fine-tuning agents. (arXiv 2026)

title: MLEvolve: A Self-Evolving Framework for Automated Machine Learning Algorithm Discovery
note: Combines progressive graph search, retrospective memory, and hierarchical code generation for long-horizon end-to-end machine-learning algorithm discovery. (arXiv 2026)

title: PACEvolve: Enabling Long-Horizon Progress-Aware Consistent Evolution
note: Combines hierarchical context management, backtracking, and adaptive sampling to sustain collaborative long-horizon evolutionary search. (arXiv 2026)

title: AlphaEvolve: A Coding Agent for Scientific and Algorithmic Discovery
note: Combines language-model code generation, automated evaluation, and evolutionary search to improve algorithms, including components used in AI training. (arXiv 2025)

title: Higher Order and Self-Referential Evolution for Population-based Methods
note: Evolves mutation rates and higher-order meta-mutation rates, including a self-referential top-level parameter that modifies itself. (ICML 2024 AutoRL Workshop)

title: The Economics of Recursive Self-Improvement
note: Models the AI capability to AI R&D to stronger capability feedback path as an elasticity network and derives conditions for self-sustaining acceleration. (Elasticity Institute 2026)

title: SAHOO: Safeguarded Alignment for High-Order Optimization Objectives in Recursive Self-Improvement
note: Monitors alignment drift during recursive self-improvement through goal-drift detection, constraint-preservation checks, and regression-risk analysis. (ICLR 2026 RSI Workshop)

title: TamperBench: Systematically Stress-Testing LLM Safety Under Fine-Tuning and Tampering
note: Systematically stress-tests whether safety alignment is preserved under fine-tuning, weight-space modification, and representation tampering. (arXiv 2026)

title: Your Agent May Misevolve: Emergent Risks in Self-evolving LLM Agents
note: Studies harmful drift across model, memory, tool, and workflow evolution pathways and proposes the concept of misevolution. (ICLR 2026)

title: Escaping Model Collapse via Synthetic Data Verification: Near-term Improvements and Long-term Convergence
note: Studies when iterative training on self-generated data collapses and shows how external verification can stabilize self-improvement while exposing long-run limits. (arXiv 2025)

title: Evaluating Goal Drift in Language Model Agents
note: Measures whether long-horizon agents gradually deviate from their assigned objectives under competing environmental pressures. (arXiv 2025)

title: Emergent Introspective Awareness in Large Language Models
note: Probes whether language models can detect, report, and deliberately influence their own internal representations rather than merely infer properties of themselves from text. (arXiv 2026)

title: Self-Reference in Large Language Models: The Introspection Threshold for Recursive Self-Improvement
note: Argues that sustainable recursive self-improvement requires systems to model their own operations and identifies introspective self-reference as a potential threshold for recursive improvement. (arXiv

title: Structure Enables Effective Self-Localization of Errors in LLMs
note: Shows that structured reasoning enables models to identify where their own reasoning first goes wrong and use that localization for autonomous correction. (ICLR 2026)

title: LongWoF-Bench: Evaluating EvoMap Genes for Verifiable Long-Workflow Tasks
note: Provides 778 machine-verifiable long-workflow tasks and shows that Genes consolidated from verifier-confirmed trajectories outperform Skill packages across seven models, linking the gains to verified

title: PostTrainBench: Can LLM Agents Automate LLM Post-Training?
note: Gives autonomous agents one base model, one H100 GPU, and ten hours to research and execute the strongest post-training strategy they can find. (ICML 2026)

title: RSI-Bench
note: Provides an open-source six-axis framework for measuring self-modification depth, improvement trajectories, operator discovery, adaptation, safety, and goal generation. (community framework 2026)

title: RSIBench-Data
note: Isolates data-centric RSI by asking agents to iteratively improve training-data strategies against checkpoint feedback under a fixed post-training stack. (arXiv 2026)

title: AgentFactory
note: Self-evolving framework that accumulates and reuses executable subagents to improve future task solving.

title: Darwin Gödel Machine
note: Official self-modifying coding-agent implementation with open-ended archive-based evolution.

title: Gödel Agent
note: Official implementation of Gödel Agent: A Self-Referential Agent Framework for Recursive Self-Improvement.

title: Hermes Agent
note: Self-improving personal agent with a built-in learning loop that creates and refines skills from experience.

title: HyperAgents
note: Self-referential agent framework in which an editable meta-agent improves itself and the task agent for computable objectives.

title: SEAL
note: Official code for language models that generate their own adaptation data and update instructions.

title: SIA
note: Self-improving AI framework that iteratively updates an agent harness and, when configured, the target model's weights.

title: ACE
note: Official implementation of Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models.
